extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines spanning four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. The questions range from humanities to science and engineering.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
extraction.citeAs: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He. C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. NeurIPS 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data is collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website (around 2000 questions with authorization).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams from the internet (primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages), past exam questions from top universities in China, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated. For questions with more than four options, incorrect choices were randomly dropped to ensure exactly four choices per question.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were initially processed into text. All questions were parsed (automatically when possible, otherwise manually by the authors) into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations, manual conversion into standard LaTeX formats was performed. All questions underwent standard data preprocessing including deduplication and cleaning. Questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all LaTeX notations were ensured to compile without syntax errors. At least around 200 questions were processed for each subject, and questions were randomly split into development set (5 exemplars per subject), validation set, and test set with a 1:9 ratio for validation and test.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Development split exemplars were annotated with explanations to enable few-shot chain-of-thought settings. Explanations were generated by combining automatic generation and human annotation: GPT-4 was prompted to generate step-by-step explanations for the ground-truth answers, then the generated explanations were manually revised by the authors to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate initial step-by-step explanations for development set questions, which were then manually revised by human annotators.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Ground-truth labels of the development and validation splits are released. Labels of the test split are kept private. Users submit model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com to automatically obtain test accuracy, where a public leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: C-EVAL is designed to help developers understand the abilities of their models from multiple dimensions and facilitate the growth of foundation models for Chinese users. The benchmark focuses on evaluating LLMs in a Chinese context, assessing knowledge of Chinese culture, history, laws, and other competencies unique to Chinese society.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark primarily targets English- and Chinese-oriented models and focuses on multiple-choice questions as a proxy for advanced abilities. The authors note that C-EVAL is far from perfect for LLM evaluation and does not cover all abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, or aspects beyond accuracy including safety, bias, and robustness. There is potential for data contamination as exam questions may be inadvertently included in LLM pretraining data, though efforts were made to mitigate this by collecting data from mock exams and local exams rather than official national exams.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating foundation models' advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities in a Chinese context. It can be used as a whole or in subsets to assess specific model abilities. The benchmark supports both zero-shot and few-shot evaluation settings, as well as answer-only and chain-of-thought evaluation modes. Use cases include: Testing, Validation.
